propositions.text: The Appellant is a citizen of Sierra Leone appealing the RPD's denial of refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX (the Appellant) is a citizen of Sierra Leone and appeals the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), denying his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant asks the RAD to set aside the RPD decision and find him a Convention refugee or person in need of protection, or refer back to RPD.
propositions.quote: The Appellant asks that the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) set aside the decision of the RPD and substitute its own decision that he is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection, or, in the alternative, refer his claim back to the RPD for redetermination.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant is a Sierra Leone citizen appealing the RPD's denial; the Appellant asks the RAD to set aside or refer back the decision.

propositions.text: The Appellant presents new evidence to the RAD showing serious possibility of persecution as a gay or perceived gay man in Sierra Leone.
propositions.quote: He has presented new evidence to the RAD that he argues establishes that he faces a serious possibility of persecution as a gay man, and/or perceived gay man in Sierra Leone.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits new evidence to the RAD about risk of persecution as a gay or perceived gay man in Sierra Leone.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed under IRPA s.111(1)(b); the RAD sets aside the RPD decision and finds the Appellant a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA)1, the RAD sets aside the determination of the RPD and substitutes its determination that the Appellant is a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal, sets aside the RPD decision, and finds the Appellant a Convention refugee under IRPA s.111(1)(b).

propositions.text: The RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness for law and fact, except for credibility of oral evidence where deference may apply.
propositions.quote: As held by the Federal Court of Appeal in Huruglica,2 the RAD must review RPD decisions on a correctness standard with respect to questions of law and findings of fact (and mixed fact and law), which raise no issue of the credibility of oral evidence.

propositions.text: Deference may be required when RPD is in advantageous position assessing oral evidence.
propositions.quote: Deference may be required when the RPD is in an advantageous position with respect to the assessment of oral evidence.

propositions.text: The RAD was able to review and understand the hearing and record; no deference applied as RPD was not in advantageous position assessing evidence.
propositions.quote: In this appeal, I was able to review and understand the hearing, as well as the record. I do not find that the RPD was in an advantageous position in assessing this evidence, and do not apply a deferential standard.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RAD's correctness standard review of RPD decisions, finds no deference applies here as RPD was not in advantageous position.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges he is gay with same-sex relationships in Sierra Leone and Canada.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that he is gay and has had same sex relationships in Sierra Leone, as well as in Canada.

propositions.text: The Appellant came to Canada in 2014 on a student visa and claimed refugee protection in February 2017.
propositions.quote: The Appellant came to Canada in XXXX 2014 on a student visa. He made a claim for refugee protection in February 2017.

propositions.text: The RPD heard the claim on July 11, 2017 and denied it in a written decision on July 24, 2017; credibility was the key issue.
propositions.quote: The Appellant had his claim heard by the RPD on July 11, 2017 and was denied in a written decision on July 24, 2017. The determinative issue before the RPD was credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges being gay with relationships in Sierra Leone and Canada; came to Canada in 2014; RPD denied claim in 2017 on credibility.

propositions.text: The Appellant's original appeal was dismissed for lack of perfection on January 24, 2018.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's original appeal was dismissed for lack of perfection on January 24, 2018.

propositions.text: The appeal was reopened by the RAD on September 26, 2018 and received by RAD on November 13, 2018.
propositions.quote: The appeal was reopened by the RAD in a decision dated September 26, 2018. The Appeal was received by the RAD on November 13, 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The original appeal was dismissed for lack of perfection but reopened by RAD in 2018 and received on November 13, 2018.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits new evidence but does not challenge RPD's credibility findings; sole issue is new evidence and refugee status.
propositions.quote: He does not challenge any of the RPD's findings on credibility. The Appellant argues that the sole issue before the RAD is based upon the new evidence and whether he should be found to be a Convention Refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits new evidence and does not challenge RPD credibility findings; sole issue is new evidence and refugee status.

propositions.text: IRPA s.110(4) allows appellants to present only evidence arising after claim rejection or not reasonably available then.
propositions.quote: Subsection 110(4) of the IRPA provides that Appellants may present only evidence that arose after the rejection of their claims or that was not reasonably available, or that they could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented, at the time of the rejection.

paragraphs.summary: IRPA s.110(4) restricts appellants to evidence arising after claim rejection or not reasonably available then.

propositions.text: RAD assesses new evidence admissibility using adapted Raza factors endorsed in Singh, excluding materiality.
propositions.quote: The RAD will apply the Raza factors, minus the "materiality" factor, as this is to be assessed in light of subsection 110(6) only.

propositions.text: Singh holds RAD should assess new evidence for credibility, relevance, and newness.
propositions.quote: In Singh, the Federal Court of Appeal (FCA) held that the RAD should assess the admissibility of the new evidence for its credibility, relevance and newness.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD uses Singh and adapted Raza factors (credibility, relevance, newness) to assess new evidence admissibility, excluding materiality.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits four new pieces of evidence related to publication of his name, photo, and personal circumstances.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits the following four pieces of new evidence that all relate to the publication of his name, photo, and personal circumstances as part of his original Appeallant's Record.

propositions.text: The evidence includes an article from Concord Times dated April 19, 2018, website printout, screenshots, and printouts from All Africa and Online Newspapers.com.
propositions.quote: * Article from the Concord Times titled "For the love of Gay..." dated April 19, 2018; * Printout of "About Us" section of the Concord Times website; * Screenshots of the above two pages on a computer; and, * Printouts from All Africa and Online Newspapers.com about Concord Times.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits four new evidentiary items about publication of his name and photo, including a Concord Times article and related printouts.

propositions.text: The Appellant's affidavit states he was informed in May 2018 that his name and photo appeared in a newspaper article about him being gay and family attacked.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits in his affidavit that accompanied his appeal record, that in May 2018 he was informed by his friend that his name and photograph appeared in a newspaper article referring to him being gay and his family being attacked.

propositions.text: The Appellant located the article in October 2018.
propositions.quote: The Appellant was able to locate the article in October 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant's affidavit says he learned in May 2018 of a newspaper article about him and found it in October 2018.

propositions.text: The new evidence meets statutory and jurisprudential admissibility tests and is accepted for consideration.
propositions.quote: I accept the new evidence and will consider it in the appeal.

propositions.text: The article dated April 19, 2018 was not available at claim rejection time, is relevant, probative, and credible as from a Sierra Leone newspaper.
propositions.quote: The article is dated April 19, 2018 and therefore, was not available, or expected at the time his refugee claim was rejected. The article and evidence related to the publication of the article is relevant and probative, as it directly relates to his claim and personal circumstances. The source is a Sierra Leonian newspaper and is therefore credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the new article evidence admissible, relevant, probative, credible, and accepts it for appeal consideration.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits new evidence post-dating his appeal under Rule 29, which considers relevance, probative value, newness, and prior availability.
propositions.quote: The Appellant also submits new evidence that post-dates his appeal. Under Rule 29 the factors to consider as to whether to allow an application include: the document's relevant and probative value; any new evidence the document brings to the appeal; and whether the Appellant could have provided this as part of the appeal record.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits post-appeal new evidence under Rule 29, which considers relevance, probative value, newness, and prior availability.

propositions.text: On January 15, 2019, RAD received further evidence including physical Concord Times copy and affidavits with IDs.
propositions.quote: On January 15, 2019, the RAD received further evidence from the Appellant. The new documents include: * Physical copy of the Concord Times newspaper dated April 19, 2018; * Affidavit of XXXX XXXX, sworn on December 10, 2018 and her ID; * Affidavit of XXXX XXXX XXXX, sworn on December 10, 2018 and her ID; * Affidavit of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX sworn on December 10, 2018 and her ID.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD received further evidence on January 15, 2019 including a physical newspaper copy and three affidavits with IDs.

propositions.text: The Appellant explains original evidence was online article; new evidence is physical newspaper and affidavits showing community knowledge of his sexual identity.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that his original new evidence was an online edition of a newspaper article, but that he was attempting to obtain a hard copy of the newspaper. This new evidence is the newspaper version. He also submits affidavits from associates indicating that they have seen the article and his sexual identity is now known in the community.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant explains new evidence includes physical newspaper and affidavits showing community awareness of his sexual identity.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits he tried to obtain this evidence before submitting his appeal record.
propositions.quote: The Appellant also submits, as part of his Rule 29 application, that he has been attempting to obtain this evidence prior to submitting his appeal record.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant says he tried to obtain the new evidence before submitting his appeal record.

propositions.text: The court accepts the new evidence as relevant, probative, and meeting statutory and jurisprudential tests, and accepts delay explanation.
propositions.quote: I accept that the new evidence is both relevant and probative, and accept the Appellant's explanations with respect to why there was a delay in obtaining these documents. I also find the new evidence meets the statutory and jurisprudential tests (subsection. 110(4) of IRPA and Singh/Raza factors).

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts the new evidence as relevant, probative, meeting legal tests, and accepts the delay explanation.

propositions.text: The court will consider the new evidence in its analysis below.
propositions.quote: I will consider the new evidence in my analysis below.

paragraphs.summary: The court states it will consider the new evidence in its analysis.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant lacked credibility on central aspects of his sexual orientation claim.
propositions.quote: The RPD found, and I agree, that the Appellant was lacking in credibility with respect to central aspects of his refugee claim regarding his sexual orientation.

propositions.text: The Appellant's oral testimony about how his family found out he was gay was inconsistent with his Basis of Claim narrative.
propositions.quote: For example, his oral testimony regarding how his family in Sierra Leone found out he was gay was inconsistent with his Basis of Claim (BOC) narrative.

propositions.text: The Appellant's testimony became more convoluted during the hearing and he could not explain discrepancies.
propositions.quote: Having reviewed the RPD hearing, the Appellant's testimony became more and more convoluted. According to his BOC he was outed after encountering his partner's ex-wife at the Yorkdale mall7. She reported it to his brother in Sierra Leone. However, in his oral testimony he recounted a different sequence of events. He was unable to explain the discrepancies.

propositions.text: His testimony about schooling and family support was inconsistent with his written evidence.
propositions.quote: His testimony was also tied to his schooling here in Canada, indicating that his brother was paying for his international student fees, which were stopped after the discovery that he is gay in 2016. However, this too was inconsistent with his written evidence8, which indicated that his schooling ended in 2015, one year before he was outed.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant lacked credibility due to inconsistent and convoluted testimony about how family learned of his sexual orientation and schooling.

propositions.text: Corroborating evidence said a man named "XXXX" disclosed the Appellant's sexual orientation to family, but the Appellant said it was a different man named "XXXX".
propositions.quote: This narrative is also inconsistent with corroborating evidence submitted indicating that the Appellant's sexual orientation was disclosed to his family by a man names "XXXX".9 The Appellant testified that it was not XXXX, but a man named XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Corroborating evidence conflicts with the Appellant's testimony about who disclosed his sexual orientation to family.

propositions.text: Other aspects of refugee claim lacked credibility, including testimony about same sex relationships in Sierra Leone and Canada
propositions.quote: There were other aspects of his refugee claim that were lacking in credibility, including his testimony about his same sex relationships in Sierra Leone and in Canada.

propositions.text: Agrees with RPD findings and reasoning as correct
propositions.quote: Generally, I agree with the findings made by the RPD, its reasoning is correct in my view.

propositions.text: New evidence is determinative
propositions.quote: The new evidence is determinative

paragraphs.summary: The court finds other aspects of the claim lacked credibility, agrees with RPD findings, and finds new evidence determinative.

propositions.text: Appeal based only on new evidence; does not challenge RPD findings
propositions.quote: The Appellant bases his appeal only on the introduction of new evidence. He does not challenge any of the RPD's findings.

propositions.text: New evidence submitted with appeal and rule 29 evidence is determinative
propositions.quote: He submits that the new evidence (both evidence that came with his appeal and the rule 29 new evidence) is determinative.

propositions.text: Agrees with appellant that new evidence is determinative
propositions.quote: I agree with this submission.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues new evidence is determinative and does not challenge RPD findings; the court agrees.

propositions.text: Examined Concord Times website and article about appellant
propositions.quote: I have examined the website of the Concord Times that the Appellant submitted. I have also considered the online article about the Appellant in both content and style.

propositions.text: Has credibility concerns about article's content and timing
propositions.quote: I have a number of credibility concerns related to the content and timing of the article.

propositions.text: Article has no byline or author, unclear how photo was obtained, published years after events
propositions.quote: The article contains no byline, there is no author associated with the article. The Appellant does not explain how his photograph was obtained or why the article is being published fours years after he has left the country, and two years after allegedly being outed.

propositions.text: Article is poorly written with grammatical and spelling errors, sentences end abruptly and do not make sense
propositions.quote: The article is poorly written; it contains grammatical and spelling errors, sentences end abruptly, and do not make sense.

propositions.text: There are multiple credibility problems with the article
propositions.quote: There are a number of credibility problems with the article.

paragraphs.summary: The court examined the Concord Times article and finds multiple credibility concerns about its content, timing, authorship, and quality.

propositions.text: Accepts that article was published online and in print and remains on Concord Times website
propositions.quote: I accept, based upon the evidence from the Appellant, that the article has been published online and in print form. It remains on the Concord Times website.

propositions.text: Article identifies appellant as gay, residing in Canada, disowned by father, family faced violence
propositions.quote: The article states the following: The Appellant is identified as a gay man; that he resides in Canada; his father has disowned him; his family members have faced violence due to the discovery of the sexual identity of the Appellant.

propositions.text: Article contains appellant's full name and photograph
propositions.quote: I see that the article contains the Appellant's full name and photograph.

propositions.text: Concord Times is a leading nationwide Sierra Leone newspaper founded in 1992 and relied on by other news outlets
propositions.quote: Other evidence submitted confirms that the Concord Times is a leading newspaper in Sierra Leone, founded in 1992 and based in Freetown. The newspaper is distributed nationwide in Sierra Leone and it is relied on by other news outlets as a source of news.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts the article was published and identifies the appellant as gay with family violence; Concord Times is a leading Sierra Leone newspaper.

propositions.text: Despite credibility concerns, new evidence establishes appellant faces serious possibility of persecution in Sierra Leone due to perceived sexual orientation
propositions.quote: I accept that the new evidence, despite the credibility concerns identified, establishes that the Appellant faces a serious possibly of persecution in Sierra Leone on account of the perception that he is gay.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds new evidence shows appellant faces serious persecution risk in Sierra Leone due to perceived sexual orientation despite credibility issues.

propositions.text: Objective evidence shows hostile socio-political environment for LGBTQ individuals in Sierra Leone
propositions.quote: The objective evidence refers to a "hostile" socio-political environment for LGBTQ individuals.

propositions.text: Discrimination is enshrined in legislation: Offences against the Person Act 1861, section 61 criminalizes buggery with penalties up to life imprisonment
propositions.quote: Discrimination is enshrined in the legislation; Offences against the Person Act 1861. Section 61"Whosoever shall be convicted of the abominable crime of buggery, committed either with mankind or with any animal, shall be liable, at the discretion of the court, to be kept in penal servitude for life or for any term not less than ten years."10

paragraphs.summary: The court notes objective evidence of a hostile environment and criminalization of buggery in Sierra Leone law.

propositions.text: National Documentation Package shows constitution offers no protection from discrimination based on gender identity or sexual orientation
propositions.quote: Other evidence found in the National Documentation Package (NDP) indicates that: The constitution does not offer protection from discrimination based on gender identity or sexual orientation.

propositions.text: Civil society groups allege law prohibiting male-to-male sexual activity limits LGBTI freedoms of expression and assembly
propositions.quote: Sexual orientation and gender-identity civil society groups alleged that because the law prohibits male-to-male sexual activity, the law limits lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and intersex (LGBTI) persons from exercising the freedoms of expression and peaceful assembly.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the constitution lacks protections and laws limit LGBTI freedoms in Sierra Leone per the National Documentation Package.

propositions.text: Appellant highlights NDP aspects showing criminalization of same-sex conduct leads to arrests of LGBTI individuals
propositions.quote: Submissions from the Appellant highlight other aspects of the NDP that address the situation for LGBTQ individuals in Sierra Leone. * The most significant human rights issues included the criminalization of same-sex sexual conduct, leading to the arrest of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and intersex individuals;12

propositions.text: LGBTI community faces discrimination, violence, denial of medical services, and no hate crime laws
propositions.quote: * Members of the LGBT community face discrimination and violence. LGBTI people are often denied medical services, and there are no laws against hate crimes based on sexual orientation;13

propositions.text: 2013 report found frequent discrimination, abuse, violence, harassment by officials, community, and families
propositions.quote: * An extensive report in 2013 concluded that "individuals in Sierra Leone are frequently subjected to discrimination and high levels of verbal abuse, violence and harassment by the public officials, members of their communities and even their own families. The combination of discriminatory laws, backed up by ignorance, lack of legal protection, and intolerance.by high rank politicians and religious leaders in public, create an environment where LGBTI individuals cannot feel safe;14

propositions.text: Sierra Leone rejected UN Human Rights Council recommendations to repeal criminalization of consensual adult sexual activity in 2014 and 2016
propositions.quote: * Sierra Leone rejected recommendations of the UN Human Rights Council to repeal all provisions criminalizing sexual activity between consenting adults in 2014 and 2016.15

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits NDP shows criminalization, discrimination, violence, and rejection of UN recommendations against LGBTI rights in Sierra Leone.

propositions.text: Appellant established on balance of probabilities that his sexual identity was exposed in Sierra Leone
propositions.quote: Given the above evidence, I find that the Appellant has established, on a balance of probabilities, that his sexual identity has been exposed in Sierra Leone.

propositions.text: No state protection or internal flight alternative exists for appellant in Sierra Leone
propositions.quote: And, based upon the objective evidence, there is no state protection or IFA for the Appellant in Sierra Leone.

propositions.text: Appellant faces more than mere possibility of persecution if returned; appeal allowed
propositions.quote: I find that he faces more than a mere possibility of persecution, if he were to return and therefore, his appeal is allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's sexual identity exposed, no protection or flight alternative exists, and allows the appeal due to persecution risk.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA, RAD sets aside RPD determination and finds appellant is a Convention refugee; appeal allowed
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(b) of the IRPA, the RAD sets aside the determination of the RPD and substitutes its determination that the Appellant is a Convention refugee. This appeal is allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD sets aside the RPD decision and finds the appellant a Convention refugee, allowing the appeal.
